text:
taylor: Heads up — after landing AWQ-quant for the new gptx-7b we started seeing flaky tool-call failures in the integra tests. Repro is intermittent but consistent on the canary pipeline. Example payloads in the logs look double-escaped:

  taylor: log snippet:
  ```
  outgoing: {
    "tool": "search",
    "args": "{\"q\":\"how to bake a cake\",\"top_k\":5}"
  }
  ```

  taylor: Essentially the tool arg that should be an object is coming through as a string containing escaped JSON. The downstream tool runtime rejects it (schema mismatch).

  aria: ugh. saw similar with AWQ when we enabled continuous batching and prefix caching together. Could be a serialization/encode path running twice. Did you try forcing the client to send structured args (Content-Type: application/json) vs string?

  sam: quick hypothesis: awq runtime path modifies the returned tokens (we do post-processing for function-call shape), and batching may coalesce chunks so we accidentally stringify an object when merging kv cache fragments. Two quick checks: 1) reproduce with batch_size=1 and no prefix cache, 2) compare raw token stream vs assembled string.

  ci-bot: smoke tests run (1904128200):
  - canary pipeline (AWQ, batch=16, prefix_cache=on): 4/50 tool-call failures (double-escaped args)
  - canary pipeline (AWQ, batch=1, prefix_cache=off): 0/50 failures
  - gptq-int8 (batch=16, prefix_cache=on): 0/50 failures

  ci-bot: full logs: https://ci.internal/reports/1904128200 (redacted)

  mona: interesting that GPTQ doesn't show it. Could be an AWQ emit hook that serializes function args into a single text token for safe transport, and that logic runs again at the aggregator. Also check streaming vs non-streaming RPC differences — streaming clients assemble incrementally and might call JSON.stringify on partial objects by mistake.

  taylor: repro steps I'm running now (if anyone can run faster on their end):
  ```bash
  ./tools/run_repro.sh --model gptx-7b-awq --batch 16 --prefix-cache on --test funcall_json_roundtrip
  ```

  aria: can you add --dump-raw-tokens and --emit-assembler-json so we can see both token-level output and assembled call? Also include sequence ids so we can line up fragments.

  taylor: added. pushing a branch with extra logging: https://git.internal/r/infra/repro/quant-emit-debug.

  sam: if we confirm it's an aggregator-level stringify, short mitigation: detect args that are parseable JSON strings and auto-parse before dispatch (temporary). Long-term: fix the emitter to keep function args as structured protobuf/JSON objects across the AWQ path. I'm happy to own the short-term patch.

  mona: let's also record accuracy delta for the different quant configs while we test (quality might hide under this). Suggest metrics to capture per-run: funcall_success_rate, json_valid_rate, avg_latency, token-cost. We'll add them to the eval dashboard.

  aria: could be related to tokenization differences too — if AWQ changes token boundaries around braces/quotes we might be inserting escape sequences. Quick test: send a minimal argument with special chars and see tokenization differences between AWQ/GPTQ/FP8.

  taylor: good call. I dumped tokenization for a failing case:
  ```
  tokens_awq: ["{","\"","t","e","x","t","\"",":","\"","foo","\"","}"]
  tokens_gptq: ["{\"text\" : \"foo\"}"]
  ```

  taylor: AWQ split quotes/braces which seems to trigger a stringify path in the emitter.

  sam: plan of action:
  - reproduce locally and confirm batch/prefix cache toggles (sam, taylor)
  - add auto-parse mitigation in router as temporary (sam)
  - add emitter-level fix to preserve structured args across assemble (aria)
  - run quant comparison sweep (AWQ, GPTQ-int8, FP8) and push metrics to eval dashboard (mona)

  aria: note for runbook: when deploying AWQ builds to Dedicated, prefer batch_size<=4 or disable prefix_cache until emitter fix lands. That will reduce throughput but avoid corrupt tool calls.

  taylor: thumbs up. I'll update the incident tracker and tag infra on the canary rollout to pause further AWQ canaries for user-facing pipelines.

  ci-bot: added incident: INC-2024-2313, linked to canary job 1904128200.

  mona: I'll schedule a small bakeoff tomorrow 08:00 PT to collect the accuracy deltas and funcall success metrics across quant modes. Please add any prompt sets to the `quant-funcall-regression` suite before midnight.

  taylor: thanks all — will post results here. :thumbsup:
